data.long_meaning: Devavrata means 'God-bound' or 'God-pledged'. In Hindu mythology, Devavrata is the name of a character who took a vow to God and lived up to it, leading a life of devotion and righteousness. The name Devavrata carries the meaning “God-bound” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devavrata usually hope their child will grow to embody god-bound and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Devavrata was a king in the Mahabharata epic. The name Devavrata carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Devavrata was the eldest of the five Pandava brothers, who were exiled from their kingdom for 13 years due to the curse of their guru. After their exile, they returned to reclaim their kingdom and defeat their cousins, the Kauravas, in the great battle of Kurukshetra.
